stories.headline: NFL Week 1: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 1.
stories.body:
The 2026 NFL season is already off to an exciting start.

In the early window Sunday, the Bears and Panthers combined for 96 points, the most in a season opener in NFL history, per ESPN Research. The Jaguars easily handled the Browns in Cleveland in quarterback Deshaun Watson's first regular-season game since October 2024. The Bills looked sharp offensively in Joe Brady's head coaching debut against the Texans, and the Lions needed overtime to get past the Saints.

In the late window, the Cardinals and Raiders won in the respective debuts of first-year coaches Mike LaFleur and Klint Kubiak. The Commanders fell despite a comeback against division foe Philadelphia. And after losing quarterback Kyler Murray to a concussion early, the Vikings scored 29 unanswered to defeat the Packers. The Giants finished things off by beating the Cowboys on Sunday night, marking the first time since 2009 both New York teams opened with a victory.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

MIA-LV | ARI-LAC | CHI-CAR

N.Y. Giants 28, Dallas 20
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
Should the Giants be taken seriously in the NFC East? This was a statement game for the John Harbaugh Giants. They looked like the better team in beating a Cowboys squad that had prevailed in 16 of its previous 18 meetings with the Giants. New York's offense looked dangerous with a power running game (165 yards) led by Cam Skattebo (18 carries, 81 yards), and quarterback Jaxson Dart was in command throughout. The defense also looked greatly improved. With neither the Eagles nor Commanders looking dominant in Week1, the Giants could be a real threat in the NFC East. For the first time in years, it's not an outlandish thought.

What to make of the QB performance: Brilliant. Dart was in control throughout, running and throwing with precision. He finished 23-of-29 for 230 passing yards with three touchdown and added 54 rushing yards. The chemistry that Dart showed all summer with new tight end Isaiah Likely translated to the opener. Likely caught eight passes on eight targets for 78 yards with two touchdowns and helped ice the game late with two big third-down receptions. -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: at Rams (Monday, Sept. 21, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Cowboys
Will this serve as a wake-up call for the Cowboys? After a drama-free offseason, the return of a top-tier offense and a revamped defense, expectations were high. Though there are 16 more games to go, the loss to the Giants showed the Cowboys have a lot of work to do. An ill-timed Dak Prescott interception at the end of the first half led to a Giants' TD. There were far too many penalties in the first half (seven, tied for the most in an opener since 2008) and a costly one in the fourth quarter, as Javonte Williams' taunting penalty led to a missed extra point attempt in a one-score game. The Giants were able to control the line of scrimmage and the clock in the second half to win a game that went according to the Giants' desired script.

Most surprising performance: Things were supposed to be different for this Cowboys defense. Not necessarily a massive move to the top of the league, but they were disappointing throughout Christian Parker's first game as playcaller. The end-of-half work that saw New York go ahead 14-7 was filled with coverage breakdowns. The second half opened with the Cowboys needing to call timeout because they had only 10 defenders on the field, and they could not come up with any stops in the final two quarters. With eight new starters from last season's opener and another handful of new key contributors, it's clear it will take time for it to come together. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. Commanders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Likely paced the Giants with eight catches -- the most by any Giants tight end in nearly three years -- with two going for touchdowns. His 27.8 fantasy points led the position, and are an indicator he'll be involved enough to be a weekly TE1. -- Cockcroft

Minnesota 39, Green Bay 22
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Vikings
What now at quarterback? For the second consecutive season, and for the third campaign in the past four, the Vikings are dealing with an injury to their quarterback. This time, new starter Kyler Murray made it only 11 plays -- and they were 11 shaky plays, at that -- before suffering a concussion at the end of a first-quarter scramble. Backup Carson Wentz, named the No. 2 quarterback last week after he was a bystander in the competition between Murray and J.J. McCarthy this summer, was understandably rusty at the outset but hung in to throw three touchdown passes and avoid a turnover. Wentz will be the starter until Murray is cleared to return.

Trend to watch: The Vikings blitzed Packers quarterback Jordan Love on nearly every first-half snap (15-of-18, or 83%), and Love burned them repeatedly en route to putting up 19 points. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores adjusted with more variety in the second half, taking down the blitz rate to 63%. It wasn't the only reason the Packers struggled to score thereafter, but it made the blitzes the Vikings did execute more effective. -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: at Bears (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Packers
Did the Packers learn nothing from last year? So much for all that offseason talk about finishing. Week 1 followed the same script from late last season: Grab the lead, make major mistakes in the second half and let the opponent back in the game. The blunders were many in this matchup: a special teams miscue (allowing a 69-yard kickoff return); a blown coverage (leaving tight end T.J. Hockenson wide open for a touchdown); bad penalties (three of them on the Vikings' go-ahead drive that wiped out a pair of would-have-been third-down stops and nullified an interception); shoddy offensive line play; and a poor coaching decision (opting to take a field goal off the board on a penalty then failing on the ensuing QB sneak).

What to make of the QB performance: Love, despite a 387-yard passing game, barely had a chance, especially down the stretch, thanks to a disastrous performance by his offensive line. Being without starting left guard Aaron Banks (knee) wasn't the reason the Vikings recorded 15 QB hits on Love; it was because the Packers couldn't handle the myriad of blitzes. When the Packers needed a fourth-quarter drive to regain the lead, Love was sacked on back-to-back plays, losing a fumble on the second one that was returned to Green Bay's 1-yard line. -- Rob Demovsky

Next game: at Jets (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Christian Watson's 32.7 fantasy points were the second most among wide receivers in Week 1 through the late window. He caught 6-of-8 targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns for the Pack. With an expanding route tree and big-play speed, Watson can be safely played as a lower-tier WR2 for Week 2. -- Bowen

Philadelphia 24, Washington 22
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Eagles
Did the Eagles' new offense pass the test Week 1? There was a boom-or-bust element to it, but the explosive plays carried them to a passing grade and a win over Washington. From WR Dontayvion Wicks' 64-yard reception (a career high) to QB Jalen Hurts' 22-yard scramble on third-and-18 to TE Dallas Goedert's 43-yard score moments later, there was plenty to be encouraged about from offensive coordinator Sean Mannion's debut. Some issues along the offensive front (left guard Landon Dickerson looked as if he was laboring) and long stretches of ineffectiveness brought back memories of 2025, but patience is required while Philly breaks in a new system.

What to make of the QB performance: Hurts threw three touchdowns, was timely with his runs and didn't commit a turnover. The pass-and-catch between the signal-caller and new WR1 DeVonta Smith along the right sideline late in the third quarter was a thing of beauty. Hurts was at his best when attacking downfield, completing 6 of 9 such attempts for 176 yards. -- Tim McManus

Next game: at Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Commanders
Did quarterback Jayden Daniels show enough to inspire a bounce-back season? Daniels looked sharp this summer in new coordinator David Blough's offense. But for most of Sunday's game -- his first since Week 14 last season -- the offense struggled against one of the NFL's best defenses. Daniels hesitated too many times because he didn't have an open target or wasn't confident in what he saw. That's concerning, as one of his best traits is being decisive. In the first half, he completed 6 of 16 passes for 43 yards. Daniels still finished strong, leading two scoring drives to nearly tie the score. But if Washington is going to avoid a bad start, Blough and Daniels need to find a better rhythm early.

Most surprising performance: Wide receiver Terry McLaurin did not catch a pass until less than five minutes remained in the contest. He finished with just two catches and four targets. It's not what Blough had in mind when he took over, saying he wanted to get McLaurin 10 targets per game. But the Eagles often doubled him, rolled coverage his way or simply blanketed him.

Best quote from the locker room: Philadelphia had four plays of 31 yards or longer that accounted for 180 of its 318 total yards, which frustrated Washington rookie LB Sonny Styles. "Those four explosives determined the game. Aside from those plays, we played pretty well. But when you put those chunk [plays] on the table, it's hard to win the game," Styles said. -- John Keim

Next game: at Cowboys (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Wicks caught just two of four targets this week, but he finished with 77 yards and a touchdown (15.3 fantasy points). He has the ability to uncover over the top, and he scored on an end zone throw from Hurts. Rostered in just 10.1% of ESPN leagues, I would add Wicks this week as a bench stash. -- Bowen

Las Vegas 27, Miami 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Raiders
Is the offensive line's performance sustainable? Yes. It's just one game, but the Raiders showed that a new coaching staff and scheme have paid dividends for the O-line. Running back Ashton Jeanty was the star, but that wouldn't have been the case without a strong performance from the players in the trenches. It will be intriguing to see if the line can translate this performance against tougher competition in the coming weeks. Two positions to monitor are left guard and right tackle. Left guard Spencer Burford gave up a team-high four pressures. Right tackle DJ Glaze allowed only one pressure on 31 pass-block snaps, which was a good sign after he struggled in 2025.

Trend to watch: Edge rusher Maxx Crosby could be on a pitch count. During the Dolphins' third drive, Crosby sat out six consecutive plays. At the league meeting in March, Las Vegas general manager John Spytek hinted at the possibility of monitoring Crosby's snap count after he underwent offseason knee surgery. Crosby totaled 1.5 sacks and seven pressures against Miami. If managing his snap count can improve Crosby's longevity, then it's a smart decision. Kwity Paye might be the one who steps up; he had two sacks and five pressures Sunday. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: at Chargers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Dolphins
How concerning is the Dolphins' offensive performance? No Miami player besides Caleb Douglas consistently got open. Game script impacted the Dolphins' ability to call run plays, but even when they rushed, ball carrier De'Von Achane was stuffed on nearly 20% of his attempts. Quarterback Malik Willis was pressured 17 times and sacked five times. Considering the Dolphins' lack of experience at wide receiver, it's fairly easy to write this off as growing pains. But the schedule doesn't get easier, and Miami's offense next gets a 49ers defense that shut down the Rams in Week 1.

What to make of the QB performance: Willis was steady, albeit unspectacular in the first half, as Miami's receivers struggled to get open downfield. Willis appeared to press a bit in the second half, highlighted by a head-scratching interception that looked more like an arm punt on second down from deep in his own territory. Willis showed a willingness to make plays with his legs, but this was a relatively uninspiring performance against what could end up being one of the Dolphins' easier matchups this season. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: at 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: The ankle injury Jeanty suffered during the preseason no longer appears to be an issue. The second-year running back scored 32.7 fantasy points, thanks in part to a pair of 13-yard receiving touchdowns. Sure, the matchup helped, but this performance reaffirmed his fantasy RB1 status. -- Cockcroft

Arizona 26, L.A. Chargers 14
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cardinals
What does an impressive upset win say about Mike LaFleur's impact on the Cardinals? Sunday certainly looked like a new dawn for Arizona under the first-year coach. It wasn't perfect, by any stretch. But the Cardinals' upset win -- they were 8.5-point underdogs on DraftKings -- showcased LaFleur's offense and all of its weapons, as Arizona moved efficiently and swiftly downfield all afternoon. Add in a few key plays by the defense at opportune times -- including a forced and recovered fumble and a blocked kick that set up a touchdown -- and suddenly a team that lost its final nine outings in 2025 looks confident for future games.

What to make of the QB performance: Jacoby Brissett played as well as anyone could've hoped in his first game in a new offense without the benefit of working through the nuances of it during OTAs or minicamp. The quarterback had one hiccup but otherwise turned in a clean and efficient performance with 277 passing yards and a touchdown on 27-for-37 passing. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: vs. Seahawks (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Chargers
Is there reason for concern about Mike McDaniel's offense? Much has been made about how explosive the pairing between quarterback Justin Herbert and McDaniel might be this season, and the O-coordinator hasn't shied away from that, saying he anticipated his receivers would have career highs across the board. On Sunday, those expectations seemed farfetched. It was the Cardinals' offense, however, that had the explosiveness with 393 total yards, as compared with L.A.'s 268. The hope for the Chargers is that they just need time to make this major offensive shift under McDaniel.

Stat to know: Coach Jim Harbaugh has gone for it on fourth down inside the 20-yard line just seven times with the Chargers, converting three. This makes Harbaugh's decision Sunday all the more surprising. With just under two minutes remaining in the second quarter and the Chargers down 10-7, Harbaugh went go for it on fourth from the 3-yard line. Defensive tackle Dante Stills sacked Herbert, and the Cardinals went on to sink a field goal to extend their lead to six points before halftime. The Chargers' 38 fourth-down attempts under Harbaugh since 2024 are tied for third fewest by any team, per ESPN Research. -- Kris Rhim

Next game: vs. Raiders (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Brissett kept the Cards' offense afloat and most notably helped tight end Trey McBride reach his eighth game of 20-plus fantasy points in their past 13 starts working together. They'll need this level of chemistry to survive one of the league's toughest schedules in 2026. -- Cockcroft

Chicago 59, Carolina 37
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bears
Can the Bears' offense be expected to overcome defensive woes all season? Their 59 points were the fourth most in franchise history. Coach Ben Johnson's goal was to have the highest-scoring offense ever and to score every time the unit touches the field; not a bad start with that goal. Chicago's 552 yards were their third most in a game in the Super Bowl era. There's plenty to clean up, from penalties to TE Colston Loveland's usage, but Caleb Williams' playmaking and a rushing attack that scored a franchise-record six TDs proved decisive. The Bears' defense, though, will need to get healthy and improve for the team to reach its overall goals.

What to make of the QB performance: Williams (21-for-29, 269 yards, two TDs, 124.1 rating) proved again his legs are legit difference makers. He recorded his first career game with multiple rushing touchdowns and was prolific when he escaped the pocket to make throws. He rushed for 65 yards on 10 carries. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Panthers
How much stock can Panthers put into an historically bad defensive performance? After spending a fortune on outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and inside linebacker Devin Lloyd in free agency, the Panthers expected their defense to be greatly improved. However, the unit was completely dismantled in an all-time horrible outing. The Panthers gave up 442 net yards and seven scoring drives before the end of the third quarter. And the 59 points scored by the Bears were the most allowed by the Panthers in franchise history. Defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero frequently came under fire during the previous three seasons. And Sunday's performance was easily his worst to date.

What to make of the QB performance: With the defense faltering all afternoon, Bryce Young did his best to keep his squad even in the opener. With offensive coordinator Brad Idzik calling plays for the first time, Young dwarfed his three previous Week 1 performances with 361 passing yards, four total touchdowns and an interception. He led six scoring drives in a shootout that Carolina ultimately lost largely because of the defense. -- Mike Kaye

Next game: at Falcons (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Williams led all quarterbacks in the early window with 37.26 fantasy points. Yes, Williams showed his rare playmaking ability as a runner, but his efficiency from the pocket was on full display as he completed 72.4% of his passes. He'll be a top-five QB in my ranks for Week 2. -- Bowen

Buffalo 36, Houston 31
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bills
Is this the version of the Bills' offense we should expect with former coordinator Joe Brady now in charge? We were promised more aggressiveness and downfield attacking, which we sure got a peek at Sunday. Of his 11 passes in the first half, quarterback Josh Allen went 6-of-7 for 149 yards and a touchdown on throws that traveled more than 10 air yards downfield, according to ESPN research. He had 11 completions of more than 10 air yards, tied for his most in a game in his career.

Stat to know: This was Allen's ninth career game with two passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns. That's five more than any other player in NFL history. Steve Young had four. Allen also became the first player in NFL history to reach 300 combined touchdowns in his first nine seasons. -- Judy Battista

Next game: vs. Lions (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Texans
How did the Texans' defense struggle so badly? It has been awhile since Houston's starting defense has allowed 30 points. The last time the unit gave up 30 in a game in which the starters finished was Christmas Day 2024 against the Ravens. Today, the offense gave them 31 points -- and usually that's more than enough for a Texans' win under coach DeMeco Ryans. A silver lining is the unit allowed only 12 points in the second half after giving up 24 in the first. But still, 36 points is unacceptable for a defense that believes it's the best.

Most surprising performance: Running back David Montgomery was viewed as a strong trade acquisition by the team, but kicking off his Texans career with three scrimmage touchdowns was impressive. Two of those came on the ground and one through the air for a total of 79 yards. It was the second game of his career with three scrimmage TDs. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: vs. Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Montgomery (28.9 points) didn't have a very efficient day running the ball (3.0 yards per carry), but the red zone usage gives him a boost. He scored twice on red zone carries (one on the goal line), and he was targeted on a schemed throw from Stroud to find the end zone. Montgomery remains a touchdown-dependent RB2 in Week 2. -- Bowen

Detroit 31, New Orleans 30 (OT)
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Should the Lions be worried about the defense, or is this what we should expect? Honestly, it might be somewhere in between, as the Saints' offense likely won't be this stellar throughout the season. When Detroit's offense struggled in the first half, the defense held the Saints scoreless and created three turnovers. But then it gave up 24 points in the second half. Edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson finished with two sacks, while S Chuck Clark and LB Derrick Barnes both snagged interceptions, but the defense was still susceptible to explosive plays. That was the same issue last year. Perhaps the eventual return of safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles) from IR will help.

Stat to know: Jahmyr Gibbs' second TD marked his 51st score in 50 career games, making him the sixth player in NFL history to reach at least 50 touchdowns in 50 or fewer games, per ESPN Research. Chuck Foreman (44 games), Steve Van Buren (45), Jim Brown (46), Larry Johnson (48) and Marcus Allen (49) round out the list.

Best quote from the locker room: Lions QB Jared Goff on tough overtime win: "I don't care how it happens. If we're up and they come back or we're down and we come back, it doesn't matter ... Yeah, of course, we'd love to keep scoring and win 49-0 of course, I'm not saying that. But listen, it's the NFL. This thing's hard. Week 1's very hard and we're happy to get a win." -- Eric Woodyard

Next game: at Bills (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Saints
What will we see from the Saints' offense next week after its slow start? It's hard to know whether the slow start in Detroit was a result of simple season-opening jitters or a true concern moving forward. The Saints took a long time to finally look right on offense. The offense came up big late and was a two-point conversion away from winning in OT, but it had too much to overcome because of its first-half struggles.

What to make of the QB performance: It was a tale of two Shoughs. He looked out of sync with the offense and had several turnovers that put the Saints in a 21-0 hole by the third quarter. But he was able to generate a lot of momentum, nearly winning the game in overtime while becoming the first Saints QB to pass for 400 yards since Drew Brees in 2018.

Best quote from the locker room: Wide receiver Chris Olave, who had a personal best 182 yards, said he was happy to be wearing a Guardian cap after he took a hard hit in practice earlier in the offseason. "Y'all know all the head injuries I done had in my career. It was just a decision I had made. I got kids now. I want to be able to live the long game. It's not all about football. I want to live regular life after I'm done with football. I love my kids to death. I don't really care how it looks no more. I just got to throw it on and shoot, it did me good today." -- Katherine Terrell

Next game: at Ravens (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Shough certainly seemed to have the skills as a passer to help fantasy managers sooner rather than later in standard 10-team formats. Coming back from two touchdowns behind, he scored nearly the entirety of his 23.2 fantasy points on the Saints' final five drives. -- Cockcroft

Baltimore 41, Indianapolis 23
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Ravens
What are the Ravens going to do at wide receiver if Zay Flowers misses any time? The Ravens may need to add a veteran receiver depending on the severity of Flowers' injury. Flowers was on his way to a career day (150 yards and one touchdown) before aggravating a left hamstring injury late in the first half, which forced him to sit out the entire second half. Flowers' injury is compounded by the loss of promising rookie Ja'Kobi Lane, who didn't play in the second half because of a wrist injury. That leaves Baltimore without its No. 1 (Flowers) and No. 3 receivers (Lane). The Ravens' only healthy wide receivers are: Rashod Bateman, LaJohntay Wester, who is primarily a punt returner, Chris Moore, who was elevated from the practice squad, and Elijah Sarratt, a rookie fourth-round pick who was a healthy scratch. Before Flowers' injury, quarterback Lamar Jackson was 10-of-13 for 214 yards and a touchdown. Without Flowers, Jackson was 7-of-12 for 110 yards.

Trend to watch: Derrick Henry's workload will remain the same. Before the season, new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle wouldn't commit to Henry getting over 300 carries for a third straight year but indicated Henry would have "an immense role." In Indy, Henry had 24 carries for 144 yards and three touchdowns. It was Henry's 26th game with more than 100 yards rushing and multiple touchdowns, which moved him past Jim Brown for the most in NFL history.

Best quote from the locker room: Jesse Minter on his first win as a head coach: "It's surreal a little bit, honestly. I don't know if it's actually hit me yet, but it's a blessing to be where I'm at. Such appreciation for the opportunity given to me by this organization." -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: vs. Saints (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Colts
Is the Colts' defense in trouble? This was a catastrophic start for a defense that was supposed to be improved, with Indy giving up its most yards since Week 8 of the 2023 season. The youth of the unit proved problematic, as Jackson exploited cornerback Justin Walley and safety A.J. Haulcy (both first-time starters) at different moments. Meanwhile, the pass rush remains a huge question. Jackson enjoyed an inordinate amount of time in the pocket, allowing his receivers to finish routes.

What to make of the QB performance: Daniel Jones was making his return to the field after sustaining an Achilles tear last December. He didn't display any obvious effects from his injury, but judging him under these circumstances will be difficult. Why? Because he got so little help from anyone else, including blockers who failed to pick up assorted blitzes and receivers who couldn't create separation. Jones was consistently under duress in the second half, given the lopsided score, and finished 19-of-31 for 166 yards. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: at Chiefs (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Doyle schemed open his playmakers in the passing game, while Jackson reminded managers about his elite dual-threat ability. Jackson threw for 324 passing yards and rushed for 41, finishing with two total touchdowns (24.96 FPTS). You can lock in Jackson as a top-two option for Week 2. -- Bowen

Pittsburgh 20, Atlanta 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Steelers
What's next with Joey Porter Jr.? It's rare that the biggest question has nothing to do with what happened on the field, but that's the case as the Steelers and Porter failed to reach an agreement on an extension by the regular-season negotiating deadline. Porter was inactive in coach Mike McCarthy's Steelers debut, though the 2023 second-round pick was spotted on the sideline wearing a gray hoodie and gray Steelers shorts. Sources told ESPN that there is a possibility of trading Porter. Once an unthinkable outcome for one of the team's up-and-coming defenders and legacy players, that possibility seems more realistic after Porter missed the game following a week of limited practice participation with a back injury. Cornerback Asante Samuel Jr. started in Porter's place, and he played well opposite Jamel Dean despite an unnecessary roughness penalty.

Trend to watch: After seeing his opportunities reduced a season ago, tight end Pat Freiermuth was Mr. Consistency for QB Aaron Rodgers. Through three quarters, Freiermuth had five catches on five targets for 46 yards. He had five catches just once last season and five-plus targets four times. Freiermuth's dependability was especially key because wide receiver DK Metcalf struggled to make contested catches. Metcalf finished with four catches on 10 targets for 40 yards.

Best quote from the locker room: Pittsburgh's T.J. Watt said he was surprised he wasn't touched, allowing him to jump up and score a 35-yard pick-six, after intercepting Rush early in the fourth quarter. "I had no idea where I was," he said. "I had no bearing at all. I'm sure the fall didn't look too graceful, but glad someone told me to get up and keep running." -- Brooke Pryor

Next game: at Patriots (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Falcons
Who will be the Falcons' quarterback in Week 2? Cooper Rush was not good in replacing Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) against the Steelers. The Falcons have classified Tagovailoa as week-to-week and Michael Penix Jr. is close to returning, he said a few days ago. Atlanta would love to have Penix back against the Panthers for Week 2. It does not seem like the team thinks undrafted rookie Jack Strand, who played great in the preseason, is ready just yet.

Most surprising performance: Kicker Nick Folk missed two field goal attempts combined over his past three NFL seasons. On Sunday, Folk missed his first two of the 2026 season, including a 45-yard attempt. The Falcons were a mess at kicker during the 2024 and 2025 seasons and were hoping Folk would be a savior. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: vs. Panthers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Best quote from the locker room: Folk didn't mince words when assessing his 45-yard field goal miss: "[That one] I just didn't hit very well. I haven't hit a kick like that in a very long time. I take full responsibility for today and just a bad day on my part." -- Marc Raimondi

Fantasy football takeaway: It's hard to imagine how badly an offense needs a healthy Tagovailoa, but that was the story of the Falcons in Week 1. Thankfully, RB Bijan Robinson managed a massive 35.3 fantasy point game and accounted for 66% of their yardage, including a heavy dose of receiving work. -- Cockcroft

N.Y. Jets 23, Tennessee 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jets
How optimistic should the Jets be? This is rarefied air for coach Aaron Glenn, who needed eight games last season to record a victory. Unlike last season, he now has a balanced offense. Consider: By the first drive of the third quarter, the wide receivers already had 148 receiving yards -- more than any game in 2025. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell delivered explosive plays while Breece Hall (102 yards) and Braelon Allen (40 yards) spearheaded a 152-yard rushing attack. QB Geno Smith, with terrific protection, played a clean game -- no turnovers, a bugaboo from last year in Las Vegas. If the Jets can stick to this formula, they could be a surprise team.

Stat to know: The defense has gone 571 pass attempts without an interception, dating to the 2024 finale -- a historic drought. Despite no picks against second-year QB Cam Ward, the defense played fantastic, making three sacks and holding the Titans to 195 total yards. They did it without safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, who left with a groin injury after six snaps. -- Rich Cimini

Best quote from the locker room: "I'm not going to write a book too early," Hall said. "We definitely left some (points) out there. I would feel a lot better if ... I wanted a little more." He said they should've scored 40 points.

Next game: vs. Packers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Titans
Will it be this hard for the Titans to reach the end zone? The first-team offense scored one touchdown on six drives in the preseason. They managed to do worse against the Jets with 10 points on nine drives. The only touchdown came in garbage time with the Jets up by 20 points. Carnell Tate's 14-yard catch in the fourth quarter was the longest offensive play of the day. New Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll stressed taking what the defense gives them, but that won't work if Cam Ward keeps missing easy throws. It could be worse next week when Tennessee hosts the Eagles.

What to make of the QB performance: Saying Ward's 2026 debut was bad is an understatement. Ward missed easy throws to RB Tyjae Spears and WR Wan'Dale Robinson near the line of scrimmage, and he failed to connect with Tate on a pass across the middle that would have been a big gain. Ward finished with 140 passing yards, though 55 came on the final drive. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: vs. Eagles (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Hall, who worked through a groin injury in camp, saw a team-high 22 carries and finished with 118 total yards and a score (19.8 points) for the Jets. He will remain a high-end RB2 next week. -- Bowen

Cincinnati 33, Tampa Bay 27
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bengals
Is the Bengals' defense as good as it appeared against Tampa Bay? It's not a mirage. There are still some aspects that need to be shored up, but the defensive line was as good as advertised. Cincinnati forced and recovered four fumbles, including a scoop and score by second-year LB Demetrius Knight Jr. for the team's first TD of the season. Cincinnati got key contributions from nearly all of its offseason signings. It was the exact impact the Bengals hoped for from a revamped defense.

What to make of the QB performance: Joe Burrow took what the defense gave him Sunday. He did a good job finding the tight ends, particularly Mike Gesicki, and working the underneath routes to move the ball down the field. The pick-six he threw in the third quarter didn't prove to be disastrous, and Burrow typically gets better the deeper he gets into a season. -- Ben Baby

Next game: at Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers
What do we make of the Bucs' four fumbles that led to 24 points? Quarterback Baker Mayfield's first fumble came while moving laterally to try to find an open receiver. The second fumble was from running back Bucky Irving, who left the ball exposed when he collided with Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy. (It's unclear if his offseason shoulder surgery played into this at all.) The third came from Mayfield while he was spinning his way out of a sack, scrambling and desperately trying to reach the end zone while in a 14-3 hole -- trying to do too much. The fourth was simply the result of Mayfield holding on to the ball too long; Mafe hit him from behind to jar it loose.

Stat to know: Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter is the first NFL rookie with a pick-six and a sack in his NFL debut since sacks became an official stat in 1982, according to the Elias Sports Bureau. He is also the ninth player in NFL history with a sack and interception in his NFL debut since 1982. -- Jenna Laine

Next game: vs. Browns (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Don't panic, Ja'Marr Chase managers: The star wide receiver had 3.2 fantasy points, but he is no stranger to slow starts. Two of his worst games have come in the past two Week 1s. And over his career, he has averaged 5.5 fewer points in September than the rest of the season. -- Cockcroft

Jacksonville 34, Cleveland 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jaguars
Is the Jaguars' Week 1 dominance sustainable? The Jaguars controlled the entirety of their season opener against the Browns, led by four touchdown passes from quarterback Trevor Lawrence. But it's the next five games that will tell us if they are actually as good as this win suggested. Four of the Jaguars' next five games are against 2025 playoff teams, beginning at the Broncos next week, Patriots at home in Week 3, at the Bengals in Week 4, and then back-to-back games in London against the Eagles and Texans. Thrive in that stretch and the Jaguars could enter their Week 7 bye as one of the best in the AFC. Time will tell.

Trend to watch: Lawrence targeted 10 players -- nine had at least one catch -- and four different players caught TDs (Parker Washington, Josh Cameron, Brenton Strange and Jakobi Meyers). Not only that, but Lawrence targeted all areas of the field. He had two TD passes of 20 or more yards, which is one shy of what he had in 2025. Having that many options in the pass game could make this offense hard to stop. -- Mike DiRocco

Next game: at Broncos (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Best quote from the locker room: Jaguars DE Josh Hines-Allen on Foyesade Oluokun's interception on the fifth offensive play of the game: "It was actually kind of crazy because the coin toss, when [the Browns] wanted to receive [the ball to start the game], I was like, 'Oh, OK.' Then we got that interception. For me ... that was the statement right there. This is when the game is going to turn that fast."

Browns
Was this just a bad game or a bad sign for the Browns? Todd Monken's first game as an NFL head coach was a worst-case outcome for a team with major question marks. Deshaun Watson looked every bit the quarterback who hadn't played a regular-season game in 693 days, while the defense looked like a unit missing edge rusher Myles Garrett and ex-defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz. Jacksonville was a tough Week 1 draw, but Sunday highlighted fundamental issues that might not be solved in a week.

What to make of the QB performance: Concerns over Watson's training camp -- inconsistent at best -- and preseason performance will only grow after this outing. In his first regular-season game since October 2024, Watson looked tentative and inaccurate throughout the game. (He went 16-of-22 with five sacks and an INT). Those are issues that predated the Achilles injury that sidelined him for all of the 2025 season. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Next game: at Buccaneers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Best quote from the locker room: Monken on Cleveland's blowout loss: "I'm not down. I'm disappointed. I mean, you're not going to get me down. Waited a long time to be a head coach in this league, man. It's freaking awesome. And we're not where we want to be, and they better get us now. We've got a young group and we just didn't play well today."

Fantasy football takeaway: The Browns, who scored 10 points and saw the opposing Jaguars D/ST score 14 fantasy points, reaffirmed their status as a top-shelf D/ST streaming target. The Buccaneers (Week 2), Panthers (Week 3) and Jets (Week 5) -- all widely available defenses -- are three of their next four opponents. -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: Max vs 100: F1 drivers predict how Verstappen will fare racing 100 drivers
stories.summary: Max Verstappen will start from the back of a 101 go-kart grid with the sole aim of reaching the front of the pack in 30 laps.
stories.body:
On Wednesday, Max Verstappen will start from the back of a 101 go-kart grid with the sole aim of reaching the front of the pack in 30 laps.

The challenge, which will be broadcast on ESPN and Disney+, will see him go up against a mix of content creators, athletes and fans on a specially designed kart track at Silverstone.

Ahead of the race, a number of Verstappen's Formula 1 rivals were asked about the four-time champion's chances of completing the challenge. Here's what they had to say...

- Max vs 100: When is Verstappen race, how to watch on Disney+, how it works, who's taking part?

- What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records

Charles Leclerc

Leclerc regularly raced against Verstappen in go-karts when they were kids, giving him plenty of first-hand experience of going wheel-to-wheel with the four-time champion. Asked what his advice would be to the 100 rivals, Leclerc urged them not to crash into Verstappen.

"I mean 100 [drivers] is a lot," he said. "Ok, that would be fun. That would be cool.

"Honestly, the only advice I'll give is maybe not to crash into Max, because he's got a season to finish. And for Max to be careful, because I don't know how professional those drivers are, but 100 drivers is quite a lot on a track, so I think it would be fun.

"But obviously when you're racing against one of the best drivers in the world, they'll probably have a tough time."

George Russell

Although he was a year ahead of Verstappen in karts, Russell has been involved in a number of intense battles with the Dutchman in Formula 1. He had little doubt Verstappen would succeed, joking that the 100 would have to think outside the box to keep him behind.

"If you go full four abreast around the whole track he might be quite difficult to protect, so maybe a couple of drivers work as a team to try and block him," Russell joked.

"I did a team race with 160 of my team members last week, and we had some top drivers, but yeah I think he should probably comfortably doing that task."

Oliver Bearman

Haas driver Bearman took part in a similar karting challenge last month when he started from the back of the grid in an attempt to overtake 50 drivers in front of him.

"I don't think Max needs any advice," he said. "But I don't know, it depends. I think it's one of those things that when I did it, I had three or four really fast drivers.

"One guy was racing in the British Championships, so when I saw him, I knew that he was going to be quick. And, obviously, there's a bit of a weight differential, so I should have prepared myself a bit more. Anyway, the more laps you do, the more chance you have of overtaking.

"I only had maybe 15 laps, so if he has double, then maybe he has a chance to do it. It's always a fun thing, but I remember it was a really cool idea on paper until I got into Turn 1 with 50 karts in front of me. And I was like, actually, this is really dangerous. But it turned out to be all good."

Carlos Sainz

Williams driver Sainz also has recent experience of starting from the back of a grid, albeit not a grid of 100...

"I did a karting race with my team and started 20th because we did reverse grid and I was P1 in five laps.

"So by my calculations, if there's another 20 times five, in 20 laps Max will be for sure P1. Fifteen, 20 laps, or who knows, depends how much overtaking there is. But he will win it easy."

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

- Madring's F1 debut left everyone dissatisfied, even Spanish GP's top 3

Gabriel Bortoleto

Audi driver Bortoleto is close to Verstappen away from the track and regularly competes against him in online sim racing. Knowing just how good Verstappen in every form of motorsport, he had little doubt that his friend would complete the challenge.

"It depends on the level of the other drivers there, obviously," Bortoleto said. "But I think there's a big chance of him winning. If I'm home doing nothing, will turn on to have fun and watch it, for sure."

Valtteri Bottas

Slightly misled by the question he was asked, Bottas seemed to think he might be offered one of the 100 karts ... and politely declined.

"If I can follow it, for sure I'll have a look. Sounds entertaining, but I'm busy next week and elsewhere, so I can't join, sadly."

stories.headline: U.S. beats France for fifth straight women's World Cup title
stories.summary: Team USA largely credited Breanna Stewart for helping guide them to the program's fifth straight World Cup title after a win over France in the final.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- For the first time in years, maybe decades, Team USA looked vulnerable entering and even during the 2026 women's basketball World Cup.

Veterans A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum were late scratches heading into the tournament. France, which nearly beat the U.S. at the Olympics in 2024, was out for blood. A three-point win against Italy in the group phase and a close call against Spain in the semifinals only made the outside noise intensify heading into Sunday's gold medal match.

The feeling was that maybe Team USA would miss out on gold at a major international tournament for the first time since 2006 and only the second time since 1994.

But as team captain Breanna Stewart sat in the news conference following Saturday's semifinal, previewing the final showdown against France, she exuded a quiet confidence.

"I've been in these games," she said at the time. "The emotional part of it is really what's going to teeter teams [for things] to not go their way. And my team, we're going to be locked in. We're going to be very composed. Doesn't matter what happens to us, we know that it's going to be a long game."

About 24 hours later, Stewart sat back in that very spot with an American flag draped around her and a gold medal around her neck, fresh off leading USA to a 97-79 victory over France. Her 22-point, 10-rebound performance in the final helped her earn World Cup MVP honors.

"I pride myself on being consistent, and that's showing up when it's the big moments and the small moments and all the moments in between," Stewart said. "It's like an unrealistic confidence that I have in myself, especially in those big moments. I believe that I always have a chance to win no matter what happens in the game."

Stewart further solidified her argument as arguably the winningest player in the sport's history, boasting four NCAA championships, three WNBA titles, three Olympic gold medals and now four World Cup golds, tying Sue Bird for the most of all time.

"It starts with Stewie," coach Kara Lawson said. "Her leadership, not just tonight, throughout the whole tournament, helping to guide the younger players, talk to them, just show them what it looks like to win.

"She is USA Basketball. When you think of the last 15 years, it's Stewie, and we're just really lucky to be a part of her era of this group."

Stewart has been a stalwart with USA Basketball for over a decade and in recent years has taken the reins alongside Wilson as pillars of this era of Team USA. But her on-court productivity and leadership had never been more important than in Berlin. The team was left with just three players -- Stewart, Chelsea Gray and Kahleah Copper -- who'd played in a World Cup before, a tournament many say is harder to win than the Olympics. Seven of the 12 had never even suited up for the senior national team in a major tournament.

Stewart ultimately led Team USA in scoring (12.8 points per game), rebounds (7.3 RPG) and efficiency rating (18.8), anchoring the defense and often even playing point guard if that's what the game required. She had her fingerprints all over the France win between a crucial 12 points in the first half to keep the USA afloat and timely plays that helped the team pull away after halftime.

"The thing that I appreciate about her the most is her willingness to do anything to help the team," Lawson said. "It's so rare in a player of her caliber.

"She will play any position for us to win, and that quality is why she's the greatest winner that we've had, probably."

Her most important contribution might have come off the court. She was the standard-bearer tasked with ensuring that this younger generation understands the expectations that come with representing the U.S. And she also had to help them navigate the pressure that comes with that.

In the weight room after the team barely beat Italy in its second game -- in what would have been one of the most shocking results the sport had seen in years -- Stewart noticed several younger players had a look of "what just happened" on their faces. She shared with them how heading into the 2014 World Cup, her first, USA lost to France in an exhibition but still went on to win the tournament.

"Stewie's been a tremendous leader through this whole process for us," Caitlin Clark said after the gold medal game. "Even after we had that close game with Italy, she was somebody that was really vocal in the locker room about, 'Don't be flustered by this. This is normal for a World Cup. You're going to have to kind of get it out of the mud at some points. It's not always going to be pretty.'"

The team's ability to internalize her message and stay the course was crucial for the remainder of the tournament, and perhaps in no situation more than when France jumped ahead by 14 in the second quarter. It was the first double-digit deficit Team USA faced in a World Cup game since the 2006 semifinal, the program's last loss in the event.

"Our group, our starters especially, when we got down big, we didn't crumble under pressure," Stewart said about the team's ability to cut the deficit to two going into halftime and then respond with a 30-12 third quarter. "[France's] run wasn't going to dictate how we were going to play the rest of the game."

Added Clark: "Stewie's a winner. All she ever does is win. She's been in so many of these moments, and when you have somebody like that on your team, it's just a really comforting thing."

Stewart didn't do it all alone -- fellow veterans Chelsea Gray, Young, Copper and Napheesa Collier also came up big against France -- but her peers recognize how special Stewart is.

"She's so skilled, man. I think sometimes you get used to seeing excellence all the time and you get complacent," said Gray, who has faced off against Stewart many times competing for WNBA championships. "You see the way she competes, the way she finishes the ball, the way she brings the team together. Things like this don't happen by accident.

"We've done it together a few times and I'm happy to share the court with her."

Added Paige Bueckers: "To see [her operate] up close and personal, it was definitely eye-opening."

The keys to USA Basketball will eventually be handed over to the likes of Bueckers, Clark, Angel Reese and Aliyah Boston, all of whom have now learned from and won with Stewart.

But as far as she's concerned, Stewart doesn't want to be done with USA Basketball -- and winning on the biggest of stages -- anytime soon.

Asked on the television broadcast if she can run it back with this group at the Olympics in Los Angeles in 2028, Stewart responded, "Oh yeah, see you in L.A.!"

stories.headline: Ballmer to accept NBA's punishment, has 'sincere regrets'
stories.summary: LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer says he is complying with the NBA's punishments of the franchise and will not pursue any legal action.
stories.body:
LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is accepting the NBA's punishments of the franchise for salary cap circumvention, he announced in a statement Sunday night.

"This has been a very difficult time for everybody associated with the Clippers, and for that, I have sincere regrets," the statement read. "I want to apologize to our fans, employees, and my fellow NBA team owners for the distraction and distress this matter has caused, for which I accept responsibility as principal owner.

"We are committing to put this chapter behind us. We have communicated to the NBA that we are complying with the penalties assessed by the league, have paid the fine, and are moving forward."

The NBA announced earlier this month a list of severe punishments for the Clippers, including the loss of five future first-round draft picks, a fine of $30 million and a yearlong suspension for Ballmer for violating salary cap circumvention rules in a case involving star Kawhi Leonard.

The punishments came down after nearly a yearlong investigation into the franchise that "found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules."

Ballmer and the Clippers initially pushed back hard on the investigation's findings, with the team saying it would challenge the league "through every avenue available to us." Ballmer's lawyer called the probe a "witch hunt" and the subsequent penalties a "gross injustice" in a letter to NBA commissioner Adam Silver. In the months leading up to the investigation's conclusion, the Clippers had remained adamant that they had done nothing wrong and expected to be exonerated.

In his statement Sunday, Ballmer said that though "there are still disagreements concerning the findings in the report," he did not want it to remain a distraction.

"Team owners should support, not distract," Ballmer said in the statement. "The challenges ahead of us are significant, but so is our resolve. We will continue to build our team and invest in our community. The confidence of our fans is our priority. With our talented roster, outstanding staff and clear vision, I am certain that we will compete at the highest level and be an organization our fans can be proud of."

The statement comes one day before the start of the NBA's board of governors meetings in New York and on the heels of a reported federal investigation into the team's alleged cap circumvention.

The Clippers will be forfeiting first-round draft picks in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033, per the league's punishment. Leonard, a two-time NBA Finals MVP, wasn't suspended but must pay the league $700,000.

stories.headline: Cris Cyborg is still going strong as a force in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: At age 41, PFL women's featherweight champion continues win streak to secure spot in ESPN P4P top 10.
stories.body:
Cris Cyborg is an MMA legend. Period. End of story.

Actually, the Cyborg story continues, even with her being 41 years old and having spent 21 years in the sport. A champion in an unprecedented five fight promotions, she has long been a fixture in the ESPN pound-for-pound women's rankings. And by posting her 30th career victory -- the most ever by a woman in MMA -- at PFL Tampa on Saturday to retain the women's featherweight championship, Cyborg solidified her hold on the No. 3 spot.

It wasn't easy, not like so many past Cyborg fights in which she aggressively bowled over opponents to score quick knockouts. Ketlen Vieira put up a fight, bloodying Cyborg's face and achieving controlling positions on the canvas several times. But Cyborg persevered, nearly doubling Vieira's strike output and earning a unanimous decision win. As a result, the ESPN voting panel kept her right where she was in the top three.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Aug. 26. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko has more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and now she's established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 4

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

9. Tatiana Suarez

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

10. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber a must-win, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Where does Aspinall go from here?

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

stories.headline: Fenerbahce coach returns to work after resignation confusion
stories.summary: Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal returned to his duties on Saturday, contradicting media reports from the day before suggesting his resignation was final.
stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal returned to his duties on Saturday, contradicting media reports from the day before suggesting his resignation was final.

Kartal had announced he was quitting his role following Thursday's draw against AS Roma in the Champions League but the club refused to accept his resignation.

Kartal, nevertheless, failed to attend training on Friday ahead of a Superlig game against Gaziantep FK.

However, Fenerbahce released a statement late Friday saying Kartal would resume his duties on Saturday for the Super Lig match against Gaziantep on Monday.

On Saturday, the club's official X account showed photos of him at work.

Kartal had resigned to the surprise of the club and its players in his news conference following the 1-1 draw with Roma to begin the Turkish club's Champions League season.

"First of all, I congratulate my players for carrying out the tasks I assigned for tonight's match to the letter. We played football worthy of the Champions League," the state-run Anadolu Agency quoted Kartal as saying on Thursday. "We could have won the match; we had clear chances. The match ended in a draw, and I am proud of my players."

Kartal continued: "Tonight, I am resigning from my position -- never to return. I extend my heartfelt thanks to my players."

In a separate news conference soon after, club chairman Aziz Yildirim said Fenerbahce fans had hurled a water bottle at Kartal, describing the incident as a reason for the coach's decision. Kartal was also upset by a series of social media posts, Yildirim said.

Yildirim insisted that Kartal's resignation was not accepted and that he would remain at the helm.

"You saw the state Ismail was in. Can a person endure that much distress?" Yildirim said. "They threw a water bottle at Ismail Kartal's head. We saw it. That is why he is upset."

"Ismail Kartal remains in his post," Yildirim added. "I said [to Kartal]: 'You will continue,' and that was that."

Despite reports in Turkey that Fenerbahce official Oguz Cetin later met with Kartal but failed to convince him to stay, Kartal is now set to take charge of the team's fixture against Gaziantep FK on Monday.

Fenerbahce is 11th in the 18-team league.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Golden Knights extend Mark Stone with 2-year, $18M deal
stories.summary: Golden Knights captain Mark Stone has signed a two-year contract extension with a $9 million annual value that goes through the 2028-29 season.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Golden Knights captain Mark Stone signed a two-year contract extension Saturday with a $9 million annual value that goes through the 2028-29 season.

He will make $9.5 million this season in the final year of his current deal.

Stone, 34, is coming off a season in which he totaled a career-high 73 points (28 goals, 45 assists) for a Golden Knights team that advanced to the Stanley Cup Final before losing to the Carolina Hurricanes in six games.

Known for boisterous goal celebrations, Stone is the emotional driver behind the Golden Knights, having played in 400 career games for the club. He also has produced, scoring 136 goals with 260 assists and a +112 rating.

Stone has 259 goals and 448 assists over a 15-year career, including more than six seasons with Ottawa before his trade to Vegas on Feb. 25, 2019.

Injuries have kept Stone from delivering even more, but he has played in at least 60 games each of the past two seasons. If Stone can stay healthy, especially going into the playoffs, the Golden Knights could make another deep postseason run with roster that includes Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner.

stories.headline: Nathan Cleary cleared to play in Preliminary Final
stories.summary: Nathan Cleary has avoided a ban for dangerous contact, with the Panthers superstar now just sweating on a foot injury ahead of Penrith's NRL preliminary final.
stories.body:
Nathan Cleary has avoided a ban for dangerous contact, with the Panthers superstar now just sweating on a foot injury ahead of Penrith's NRL preliminary final.

Cleary was on Monday handed a grade-one dangerous contact charge for collecting Hugo Savala's leg after the Sydney Rooster kicked in Penrith's 19-12 qualifying-final win.

But that charge only carries with it a $1000 fine with an early guilty plea, meaning Cleary can breathe a sigh of relief with no ban in place.

However AAP understands the two-time Clive Churchill Medallist is set for scans on his right foot late on Monday, with that injury still threatening his finals series.

After kicking a match-winning field goal late in Sunday's win, the Penrith halfback could be seen telling a Panthers physio "my foot is f***ed".

The 28-year-old appeared to suffer the injury moments before that drop kick, and opted to give Dylan Edwards the Panthers' last conversion attempt near fulltime.

Cleary did attempt to play down the injury to his right foot after the game, but his father and coach Ivan admitted there was "something wrong with it".

"I just copped a little bump on the foot," Nathan Cleary said on Fox League.

"It was a pretty important kick, so I just wanted Dyl (Edwards) to take it. I wasn't sure how it would hold up goal kicking.

"It was just precautionary."

Even if Cleary has suffered damage to his foot, it is likely Penrith would be able treat or numb the injury and have him play the Warriors or Newcastle in the preliminary final.

But what impact that treatment may have on his ability to kick and step would remain in question.

The Panthers already have captain Isaah Yeo playing through a ruptured pectoral muscle, after he delayed surgery to return ahead of the finals.

Meanwhile the match review committee's call to hand Cleary a grade-one charge has saved Penrith weighing up a monumental decision.

Had Cleary been handed a grade-two charge, the Penrith halfback would have been facing a one-game ban and the reality of being rubbed out of the preliminary final.

Manly prop Josh Aloiai and South Sydney forward Jacob Host received grade-two charges in 2024 for making contact with kickers.

Canberra's Zac Hosking was fined for a similar incident in last year's finals, while Melbourne's Harry Grant had a charge overturned at the judiciary in 2024.

Cleary could have attempted to fight a ban at the NRL judiciary, but would have risked having the suspension double and include the grand final if he lost.

For now, Penrith don't have to worry about that gamble. But another one may still need to be weighed up on Cleary's foot.
